rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Second Card Effects 4 Game End Overview Get rid of your Fleas and collect cats Turn On your turn, play 2 cards First card does NOTHING Second card will have an effect based on how it's played Second Card Effects Normal or Scratch added to Stack - Take all cards on the immediate adjacent spaces Normal or Scratch added to Empty - Discard fleas equal to the number of connected adjacent cards in a sequence including itself Scratch (black border) bonus - Give each opponent fleas from the supply equal to the number of cards in the space regardless of whether they are Scratch or Normal. e.g. a Scratch added to an empty space means there is now one of that number so everyone else takes 1 Flea. A Scratch added to a pile of two before it, means there is now three in that pile and so everyone else takes 3 Fleas Game End When either a player cannot draw cards at end of turn or a player runs out of Fleas, the game ends Except for the Game Ender, everyone else takes a final turn Each collected Cat is a point Fleas gain you points if under 11 Fleas lose you points if over 15 Fleas neither gain nor lose if 11-15 The player with the most points wins! If tied, the tied player with the least Fleas wins!

[Rating: 4/10] Played on BGA.  Light card game with non-intuitive rules and not many interesting decisions.

[Rating: 5/10] Light card game trying get rid of bugs by completing runs of cards. It is lucky, party-type game. Not really something I would play.

[Rating: 5/10] [b]Abstract card game where you are trying to shed negative tokens that you start the game with while also picking up positive points by collecting cards[/b]  + I like the core gameplay well enough; a lot of it is about limiting opportunities for your opponent + The two pronged scoring is interesting (shedding your fleas vs. scoring points) + I always like the subtle decision of when do I topdeck  - The scratch cards inject a little too much randomness - The scoring balance feels a little off - it's kind of trivial to prioritize - The deck makeup isn't symmetrical which makes it more difficult

[Rating: 5/10] W grze Scratch & Catch próbujesz pozbyć się pcheł. Gracz dokłada dwie karty, z czego pierwsza nic nie robi, a druga albo bierze wszystkie sąsiednie karty albo pozwala odrzucić pchły. Cała zabawa polega na zarządzaniu kartami, zbieraniu ich i tworzeniu sekwensów, by móc pozbywać się pcheł. Gra jest szybka i przyjemna do rodzinnego pogrania, ale bez polotu. Można zagrać, na pewno nie muszę mieć jej w kolekcji.
